Retry the failures of a bulk Wayback run

Source: R/wayback_save.R
wayback_retry.Rd

Reads the results file a wayback_save run wrote and tries again every URL whose latest result is "failed" (or "submitted": a capture a stopped run had started, which is polled rather than submitted again), so nobody has to dig the failures out by hand. Each failed URL is first looked up in the Wayback Machine, one lookup a second: a capture made at any time (an earlier one of a page that has since gone, or one made today by another run when the daily limit refused this one) is recorded as "existing" without capturing again. What is left is captured again with wayback_save(), appending to the same file. A page its source no longer has (HTTP 404 or 410, "cannot find") is not sent again unless include_gone = TRUE: a new capture would only archive the error. A failure for a daily limit recorded today (UTC) is not sent again until tomorrow.

Usage

wayback_retry(output, include_gone = FALSE, lookup = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

output

The JSON Lines results file of an earlier wayback_save() run (or of rmbl wayback); results of the retry are appended to it.

include_gone

Also capture again the pages whose failure says the page is gone.

lookup

Look each failure up in the Wayback Machine before capturing again.

...

Passed to wayback_save(): jobs, within, the keys, quiet, per_minute, max_captures.

Value

The whole run as it now stands, one row per URL (a data frame of class rmbl_wayback_save), with the attribute retry: how many failures there were, how many a lookup found, how many were captured again, how many were left as gone, and how many were left for tomorrow (a daily limit hit today).

See also

wayback_save; rmbl wayback --retry FILE.jsonl from the command line.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- wayback_save(urls, output = "snapshots.jsonl")
# later, or the next day once the daily capture limits have reset:
res <- wayback_retry("snapshots.jsonl")
attr(res, "retry")
} # }
